q: The reaction-diffusion equation uₜ = DΔu + f(u) (D > 0, f satisfies a dissipativity condition) on a bounded domain has a global attractor 𝒜 in H¹₀(Ω). The key step in proving compactness of 𝒜 uses:
opts: Compact Sobolev embeddings: H¹ ↪ L² is compact (Rellich-Kondrachov), which converts H¹-boundedness to L²-precompactness
exp: The compact embedding H¹(Ω) ↪ L²(Ω) (Rellich-Kondrachov) is the key: solutions bounded in H¹ (from energy estimates) form a precompact set in L². This gives the compact absorbing set needed for the global attractor theorem.
